video.title: AI-Assisted Coding Tutorial – OpenClaw, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, CodeRabbit, Gemini CLI
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (1:14:43–1:16:13), CO1.LO3 ✓ (0:45–3:44) [from transcript] · freeCodeCamp.org · tier 2 · 1:25:26 · 286,323 views · captions
video.description:
Learn how to use AI tools to become more productive as a developer.

You will master AI pair programming and agentic terminal workflows using top-tier tools like GitHub Copilot, Anthropic's Claude Code, and the Gemini CLI. The course also covers open-source automation with OpenClaw, teaching you how to set up a highly customizable, locally hosted AI assistant for your development environment. Finally, you will learn how to maintain high code quality and streamline your team's workflow by integrating CodeRabbit for automated, AI-driven pull request analysis.

Some of this course is based on this article from Mrugesh Mohapatra:  https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/how-to-become-an-expert-in-ai-a

review.review: Comprehensive tutorial on modern agentic workflows and multi-tool strategies. Excellent for flipped class or hands-on lab exercises on contextualizing AI tools across the development lifecycle.

video.title: My AI Coding Workflow That Actually Works
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (0:00–1:30), CO1.LO3 ✓ (0:00–1:30) [from transcript] · Chris Titus Tech · tier 4 · 25:17 · 45,041 views · captions
video.description:
Most people use AI coding agents by giving them one giant prompt and letting them run wild. That might work for a tiny project, but it quickly falls apart when you are building real software.

In this video, I walk through my complete AI development workflow using agents, specifications, roadmaps, testing, pull requests, CI, security scanning, and independent code reviews. I also demonstrate the process on a real project, from the initial request through review, fixes, validation, and the final merge.

The model matters, but your workflow matters more. Manual gates, clear acceptance criteria, small pull requests, and proper testing are what turn AI-generated code into maintainable software.

video.description:
Most people use AI for one thing: writing code. But coding is just one step in a seven-stage process that every piece of software goes through. AI can accelerate all of them.

In this video I walk through the full software development lifecycle, stage by stage, and show you exactly where AI fits into each one.

What you'll learn:

- Why skipping the planning stages is killing your AI coding results
- How to use AI to write better requirements and technical designs
- Why coding is Step 4, not Step 1
- How to brief a coding agent properly for dramatically better output
- Why self-review catches bugs that generation misses
- How AI can help you deploy and monitor, not just build
